examples.english: Marielys Valdéz, inspector general of the Supreme Court of Justice, warned that "puputovs" are "biological weapons" and their use carries high penalties.
examples.ref: 2017 May 11, “‘Puputov’: las bombas de excrementos que son el último recurso de algunos manifestantes en Venezuela que protestan contra el gobierno de Nicolás Maduro”, in BBC Mundo:
examples.text: Por su parte, Marielys Valdéz, inspectora general de tribunales del Tribunal Supremo de Justicia, advirtió que el uso de las "puputov" son "armas biológicas" y tienen penalidades altas.
examples.translation: Marielys Valdéz, inspector general of the Supreme Court of Justice, warned that "puputovs" are "biological weapons" and their use carries high penalties.

examples.english: On 11 May a new non-conventional weapon debuted in Caracas, used by young opposition members to “resist” the police and military arrayed against them: the puputov. The name of this new “armament” is inspired by the Molotov cocktail, and they consist of glass jars filled with human or animal excrement.
examples.ref: 2018 April 2, “Los casos más memorables ocurridos en Venezuela durante las protestas”, in El Estímulo:
examples.text: El 11 de mayo debutó en Caracas un arma no convencional utilizada por jóvenes de la oposición para hacer “resistencia” a los policías y militares que enfrentan en las calles: la puputov. El nombre de esta nueva “arma” estaba inspirado en los cócteles molotov y son tarros de vidrio o bolsas cargadas con excrementos humanos o de animales.
examples.translation: On 11 May a new non-conventional weapon debuted in Caracas, used by young opposition members to “resist” the police and military arrayed against them: the puputov. The name of this new “armament” is inspired by the Molotov cocktail, and they consist of glass jars filled with human or animal excrement.

examples.english: EFE found that while the National Guard used tear gas and high pressure water jets to disperse the protesters, a group on the motorway above Bello Monte (east) responded with stones, bottles of paint, and jars filled with excrement, known in the country as "puputov cocktails".
examples.ref: 2020 March 2, EFE, “La violencia se cobra otra vida en Venezuela tras 40 días de protestas”, in Noticias de Gipuzkoa:
examples.text: Efe constató que mientras los efectivos de la Guardia Nacional lanzaban los gases lacrimógenos y chorros de agua a presión para dispersar la protesta, a la altura de Bello Monte (este) de la autopista, un grupo de manifestantes respondía con piedras, botes de pintura y tarros de excremento, conocidos ya en el país como cócteles "puputov".
examples.translation: EFE found that while the National Guard used tear gas and high pressure water jets to disperse the protesters, a group on the motorway above Bello Monte (east) responded with stones, bottles of paint, and jars filled with excrement, known in the country as "puputov cocktails".

glosses: a bottle filled with faeces thrown as a weapon
